item.title: Urban memory and mental health
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00526-9

To what extent does the memory of historic urban spaces benefit the mental health of lifelong residents? A new experimental study used multimodal psychophysiological measurements and revealed that urban memory could significantly improve mental health in older lifelong residents. This News & Views discusses the methodology and findings of this study to stimulate further research and practice on this critical and timely topic.
item.dc:title: Urban memory and mental health
item.dc:creator: Bin Jiang

item.title: Revisiting the urban past virtually to enhance well-being for older adults
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00523-y

As development progresses, urban landmarks may be lost to history, resulting in the disconnection and isolation of older adults from their contemporary city. Huang and colleagues virtually reconstructed immersive past urban scenes from Hong Kong to understand the physiological and psychological effects and support mental health for aging populations.
